What we are implementing

Reviews on autopilot. Reputation under control.

Right now a 5.0★ listing is a real advantage — and a fragile one. Crews forget to ask. Happy customers never post. One frustrated customer can, because nobody caught it first. Review Shield hooks the Voixly / WordPress CMS so the ask happens every time, and the first rating never hits Google or Yelp until it should.

How vetting actually works: Nothing is auto-posted to Google or Yelp. The customer always writes the public review on those sites. What we control is the first screen. Happy jobs get the public-review invite. Unhappy jobs never see those buttons — they go to a manager queue at (281) 541-0027 so the issue is handled in-house first.

The system

From job complete to Google — with a checkpoint

Five steps. No extra work for the field. The office only gets pulled in when a rating comes back low.

01

CMS trigger

Job marked complete in Voixly / WordPress (or the production system). Customer name, phone, email, city, and job type sync over.

02

Auto ask

Same-day SMS + email from Core Four. One link. Ten seconds. No “please leave us a Google review” on the first screen.

03

Private score

Customer taps 1–5 stars on a branded Core Four page. That score is yours. It does not publish.

04a

Happy path

4 or 5 stars: “Share that on Google / Yelp.” Direct links to the Tomball listing and Yelp page.

04b

Recovery path

1–3 stars: “Tell us what happened.” Manager text + email. Google and Yelp stay hidden.

Low scores stay in the dashboard as service-recovery tickets. Those do not become Google or Yelp reviews unless the customer later chooses to post on their own — we simply don’t hand them the link while they’re unhappy.

Happy reviews go public

Maria’s 5★ private score unlocked Google and Yelp. She wrote: “Crew showed up when they said they would and the Cypress building is dry.” That is a real review, on Google, from a real job — just asked at the right moment.

Bad scores get vetted

James hit 2★ because a leak stain wasn’t fully cleaned. No Google button. Office called the same day, sent a crew back, and closed the ticket. That 2★ never became a 2★ on the listing.

Commercial jobs included

The Humble warehouse and Spring strip are in the same pipeline. Property managers get the same private rating. High scores feed the commercial listing story you are already building in search.

90-day rollout

How we turn this on

Built on the Voixly CMS you already use, branded like the rest of this report, and wired to the Tomball Google listing and Yelp page.

1

Days 1–14 — connect the CMS

Job-complete trigger from Voixly / WordPress (name, phone, email, job type, city). Branded rating page. Google review link for the Tomball GBP. Yelp link. Office alert to (281) 541-0027 and the shop email.

2

Days 15–30 — private rating live

Every completed job sends the SMS + email. 4–5★ get Google/Yelp. 1–3★ go to the recovery queue with a same-day callback rule. No public posting by us — ever.

3

Days 31–60 — prove the shield

Weekly dashboard: requests sent, ratings in, public reviews posted, issues held. Tune copy. Add a 3-day reminder only for people who never tapped the first link.

4

Days 61–90 — make it habit

Office owns the held queue like a punch list. New Google/Yelp reviews get a thank-you reply. The 5.0 stays protected because unhappy work is caught before the listing is invited.

What we are implementing, in one line: When a Core Four job is marked complete in the CMS, the customer is asked for a private rating. Four and five stars are invited to Google and Yelp. One to three stars are held for the office so bad reviews can be vetted — and fixed — before anyone is sent to a public site.
